items.cite: Richard Osborne, *Rossini: His Life and Works*, 2nd ed. (Oxford University Press, 2007).
items.note: Osborne covered the whole career and its music, including the decades after William Tell and the place of the serious operas beside the comedies.

items.cite: Emanuele Senici, ed., *The Cambridge Companion to Rossini* (Cambridge University Press, 2004).
items.note: The book examines how these operas were assembled for particular theatres and singers, with chapters on librettos, compositional methods, ornamentation, staging and editing.

items.cite: Philip Gossett, *Divas and Scholars: Performing Italian Opera* (University of Chicago Press, 2006).
items.note: Gossett discusses the editorial decisions that shape a Rossini performance: which version to perform, what to cut and how far a singer may ornament.

items.cite: Fausto Petrella, ‘Spazio artistico e umorismo in musica. Il comico musicale e i suoi rapporti con il Witz’, *De Musica* 7 (2003).
items.note: Section VIII examines how strictly organised singing in ensembles from The Barber of Seville, La Cenerentola and L’italiana in Algeri can sound like collective confusion. In Italian.
